title: wheelgap --json report
description: The object printed by `wheelgap --json` from report_json() in src/wheelgap/cli.py. This schema does not cover `--list-targets --json` or the `{"error": ...}` object printed on input errors. It describes the output of the wheelgap version it ships with: later versions may add keys, so a saved copy can reject newer output.

version.description: The wheelgap version that produced this report.

sources.description: Labels of the inputs that were checked (lockfiles, requirements files, or package names).

targets.description: The platforms and Pythons that were checked. Each package's results, rejected and via keys are these labels.

label.description: Key used in results/rejected/via: the platform alone when one Python is checked, or 'PYTHON PLATFORM' when several are.

python.description: Python version, with a trailing t for free-threaded builds.

platform.description: Platform name such as linux-x86_64 or musl-aarch64.

packages.description: One entry per package that is installed on at least one target. A range that resolves to different releases for different Pythons has one entry per release, with n/a for the targets using the other.

skipped.description: Packages that were not looked up (git, path, file, editable, private index, …).

ignored.description: Package names excluded by --ignore or ignore = [...] in [tool.wheelgap].

ignored_targets.description: Present from 0.9.0 on (older versions don't write it): packages ignored on some targets only, by --ignore NAME:TARGET or the same form in ignore = [...]. They stay in packages with their real results, but a gap on these platforms doesn't count towards with_gaps or the exit code. Lists only checked platforms, and no package that is also in ignored.

name.description: Package name as written in the input.

platforms.description: Platform names (as in targets[].platform), for every Python checked on them.

advisory.description: Present in versions after 0.9.0 (0.9.0 and older don't write it): labels of the checked targets that --advisory or advisory = [...] in [tool.wheelgap] made advisory, empty when there are none. Gaps on these targets are reported in packages and counted in with_gaps and per_target as usual, but don't change the exit code.

blocking_newer_python.description: Present only when exactly two Python versions are checked and one is newer (3.14 and 3.15, or 3.14 and 3.15t; not 3.14 and 3.14t), and not written by 0.9.0 and older: the packages that block the move to the newer one, in the order of packages. A package is listed when the newer Python's result is source or missing on a platform where the older one's is wheel, n/a or bundled, not counting the platforms in ignored_targets. It's decided per package name, over every version of it in the inputs. Packages that couldn't be checked (unknown on the newer Python) are left out, so an empty list isn't a pass on its own: summary and the exit code still decide.

items.description: Package name as written in the input.

with_gaps.description: Packages whose results include source, missing or unknown, not counting the platforms in ignored_targets. Gaps on advisory targets count.

per_target.description: Gap counts for every checked target, keyed by target label, with zeros for a target without gaps (including when only one target is checked). A package's cell on a platform ignored_targets lists for it isn't counted. Present from 0.9.0 on; older versions leave it out.

source.description: Packages that build from source on this target.

missing.description: Packages that can't install on this target.

unknown.description: Packages wheelgap couldn't check for this target.

name.description: Package name as written in the input.

version.description: Pinned or resolved version, if known.

error.description: Why the package is unknown, otherwise null.

results.description: Status for each target, keyed by that target's label.

rejected.description: Present with --explain: rejected wheels and reasons, keyed by target label, only for targets whose result is source or missing and that ignored_targets doesn't list for this package.

via.description: Present with --explain: dependency path that installs the package, keyed by target label, for the same targets as rejected (uv.lock, and poetry.lock before lock-version 2.1). Empty object when the input has no graph.

build_requires.description: Present in versions after 0.9.0 (0.9.0 and older don't write it), with --explain --build-info: the [build-system] requires of the release's sdist, normalized (name, extras, version range) and limited to those whose marker holds on a target in rejected that is source; null when there is no source build or no answer (the sdist isn't positively from PyPI, couldn't be read, or pip could read another pyproject.toml from it).

notes.description: Present in versions after 0.9.0 (0.9.0 and older don't write it), with --explain: the coverage tracker's notes (https://github.com/wheelgap/tracker/blob/main/notes/README.md) that apply to this package's gaps, each with the gap targets it covers. Only looked up with --notes (or notes = true), for packages that are positively from PyPI, and never with --offline, --index-url or a WHEELGAP_INDEX_URL mirror. Empty without --notes, when there are none, or when the lookup failed. Treat text as untrusted plain text.

platforms.description: Platforms the note is about, or ["all"]: the nine platforms the tracker scans.

text.description: One line of plain text; backticks mark commands and names.

links.description: https:// URLs that back the note.

versions.description: The releases the note is about (a version specifier), or null for all.

updated.description: When the note was last checked (YYYY-MM-DD).

targets.description: The labels of this package's gap targets the note covers.

conda_forge.description: Present with --explain --conda-forge, in versions after 0.9.0, when conda-forge has a package with exactly this package's canonical name and a build of this version that fits at least one of the targets in rejected: on the main label and not marked broken, for the target's conda subdir or noarch, and for its Python version and ABI (free-threaded or not). A hint only: it doesn't change results, summary or the exit code, and the conda package may be another project. Left out when nothing fits, the package's index isn't known to be PyPI (its name isn't sent), or the lookup failed (a note on stderr says so).

name.description: The conda-forge package name that was looked up (the canonical PyPI name).

version.description: The checked version, which every build counted is of.

builds.description: For each target label with a build that fits: the conda subdirs of those builds, its own (such as linux-aarch64 or osx-arm64) and/or noarch.

bundled.description: Present with --pyodide-lock when this package is bundled on a Pyodide target: the version Pyodide ships.

bundled_version_differs.description: Present with bundled: true when Pyodide's version isn't the one pinned, or is outside the required range (it still counts as bundled). Always false for an unpinned requirement.
